description: We are a student group from a science high school in Turkey. Teamwork and software is primarly what we are looking for.
summary: Callow Astronaut: The Mars Mission is an educational game developed and completed to convey to children aged 10-16 what it means to be an astronaut on Mars, through an interactive story and a mission simulation. Players take on the role of a young astronaut who has reached Mars, managing base life, exploring the environment, and making critical decisions when faced with unexpected situations. The decisions made directly affect the status of vital resources such as oxygen, and the player is given three chances to make a mistake. In the project, scientific knowledge is not merely conveyed; rather, the player is given the opportunity to think and make choices using this knowledge.
details:
Callow Astronaut: The Mars Mission is a browser-based, first-person educational game that puts the player in the gloves of a young, inexperienced (“callow”) astronaut on their first day on Mars. Players guide the astronaut through a crew check-in, the landing, surface operations, a sudden dust storm and a sample collection task, while keeping an eye on oxygen, suit temperature and lives. Along the way, mission control explains real Mars science. For example, Mars gravity is only about 38% of Earth’s, so jumps reach much higher, and dust storms can grow huge but their winds push far less than winds on Earth because the atmosphere is only about 1% as dense.

Our goal is to make NASA’s Mars science something students can not just read, but also play. Players learn accurate facts, feel what a first mission is like, and become more curious about Mars exploration. The game runs in any browser, on computers and phones, with no installation, so it is easy to use in classrooms and to share.

We built the game with HTML5 Canvas, JavaScript and CSS in a single self-contained file. The backgrounds use real NASA Mars rover photographs, and the interface uses Google Fonts (Orbitron and Exo 2).

The project is creative in several ways. The astronaut’s arms are our own hand-drawn artwork, placed over real photos of Mars so players see the real surface through the astronaut’s eyes. We built our own dust system with layered, drifting clouds for the landing and the storm. The main character is a beginner, so learning is part of the story itself.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility on different devices, readability (translucent text panels that keep the scenery and the astronaut’s arms visible), and clear, age-appropriate language.
